items.title: Desiderius Erasmus (c. 1466–1536)
items.meta: Early Tudor & Humanist Reformation · European Literature in Translation · 1 PYQs

fields.label: Writer Name
fields.value: Desiderius Erasmus

fields.label: L1 One-Line Flash Anchor
fields.value: Praise of Folly (written 1509; first printed 1511); Colloquies grew through editions from 1518.

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Desiderius Erasmus was a Dutch priest, teacher, and the most famous scholar of his age. He was born in Rotterdam about 1466 and died in Basel in 1536. He wrote in Latin, not in English. He wanted the church reformed by learning, clear scripture, and peace.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET asks Erasmus under Unit IV (prose that is not a story). Questions match Praise of Folly with 1511 and the Colloquies with 1518. A common trap is to call him an English poet.

fields.label: Memory Tip & Exam Traps
fields.value: Erasmus, about 1466 to 1536: Folly written in 1509, printed in 1511. | Praise of Folly (written 1509; first printed 1511); Colloquies grew through editions from 1518. | Latin. Not English literature.

items.title: Thomas More (1478–1535)
items.meta: Early Tudor & Humanist Reformation · British & Irish Literature · 5 PYQs

fields.label: Writer Name
fields.value: Thomas More

fields.label: L1 One-Line Flash Anchor
fields.value: Latin edition 1516; English translation 1551, posthumously.

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Thomas More was an English lawyer, writer, and statesman. He was born in London in 1478 and was beheaded in 1535. He served Henry VIII as Lord Chancellor from 1529 to 1532. He refused to accept the king as head of the Church.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: Unit 3 (Fiction) and Unit 4 (Non fictional prose). Questions test the Latin date 1516, the English date 1551, and the two books.

fields.label: Memory Tip & Exam Traps
fields.value: Latin Utopia in 1516. English by Ralph Robinson in 1551, after More's death. | Latin edition 1516; English translation 1551, posthumously. | Latin, 1516.

items.title: Thomas Elyot (c. 1490–1546)
items.meta: Early Tudor & Humanist Reformation · British & Irish Literature · 1 PYQs

fields.label: Writer Name
fields.value: Thomas Elyot

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Sir Thomas Elyot was an English scholar, diplomat, and prose writer. He was born about 1490, and he died in Cambridgeshire in 1546. He served as clerk of the Privy Council (the king's group of advisers). He was knighted in 1530, and in 1531 he went as an envoy (a royal messenger) to Emperor Charles V.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: Unit 4 (non fictional prose). Questions test 1531 and the education of the governor. They also ask for an early English book on how to train rulers.

fields.label: Memory Tip & Exam Traps

items.title: William Tyndale (c. 1494–1536)
items.meta: Early Tudor & Humanist Reformation · British & Irish Literature · 6 PYQs

fields.label: Writer Name
fields.value: William Tyndale

fields.label: L1 One-Line Flash Anchor
fields.value: New Testament (1526); revised edition (1534); Pentateuch (1530). Translation was printed abroad; dates differ by edition.

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: William Tyndale was an English scholar, Bible translator, and Protestant martyr. He was born in Gloucestershire about 1494. He studied at Oxford and at Cambridge, then translated Scripture abroad because England would not allow it. He was strangled and burned at Vilvoorde, near Brussels, in 1536.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET asks Tyndale in Unit 4 (non fictional prose). Questions test 1526 for the New Testament and 1530 for the Pentateuch. They also ask how his English shaped later Bibles.

fields.label: Memory Tip & Exam Traps
fields.value: New Testament 1526, revised 1534. Pentateuch 1530. Death in 1536. | New Testament (1526); revised edition (1534); Pentateuch (1530). Translation was printed abroad; dates differ by edition.

items.title: Thomas Wyatt (c. 1503–1542)
items.meta: Early Tudor & Humanist Reformation · British & Irish Literature · 2 PYQs

fields.label: Writer Name
fields.value: Thomas Wyatt

fields.label: L1 One-Line Flash Anchor
fields.value: Poems circulated in manuscript during his lifetime; first major printed collection, Tottel’s Miscellany, 1557, after his death.

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Sir Thomas Wyatt was an English poet and diplomat at the court of Henry VIII. He was born about 1503 at Allington Castle in Kent. He died of a fever in 1542 at Sherborne. With the Earl of Surrey, he brought the sonnet (a poem of 14 lines) into English.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET asks Wyatt under Unit II (Poetry). Questions match him with the English sonnet, Petrarch, and Tottel's Miscellany. They also ask for lines from They Flee from Me and Whoso List to Hunt.

fields.label: Memory Tip & Exam Traps
fields.value: Wyatt, about 1503 to 1542: sonnets after Petrarch, printed in Tottel in 1557. | Poems circulated in manuscript during his lifetime; first major printed collection, Tottel’s Miscellany, 1557, after his death.

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Roger Ascham was an English scholar and a teacher of Latin and Greek. He was born about 1515 at Kirby Wiske in Yorkshire. He died in London in 1568. He taught Princess Elizabeth, and he later served Queen Mary and Queen Elizabeth.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: Unit 4 (non fictional prose). Questions ask 1545 for Toxophilus and 1570 for The Scholemaster. They also ask about double translation and about Elizabeth's tutor.

items.title: Henry Howard, Earl of Surrey (c. 1517–1547)
items.meta: Early Tudor & Humanist Reformation · British & Irish Literature · 0 PYQs

fields.label: Writer Name
fields.value: Henry Howard, Earl of Surrey

fields.label: L1 One-Line Flash Anchor
fields.value: Poems printed in Tottel’s Miscellany (1557), posthumously; early English blank verse in his Aeneid translation.

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Henry Howard, Earl of Surrey, was an English courtier and poet. He was born about 1517 at Hunsdon in Hertfordshire. Henry VIII had him beheaded for treason in 1547. With Thomas Wyatt, he brought Italian verse forms into English.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: Unit 2 (Poetry). Questions ask who shaped the English sonnet and who first used blank verse in English. They also ask for Tottel's Miscellany in 1557 and for his death in 1547.

fields.label: Memory Tip & Exam Traps

items.title: George Puttenham (c. 1529–1590)

fields.label: Writer Name
fields.value: George Puttenham

fields.label: L1 One-Line Flash Anchor
fields.value: 1589; important Renaissance account of poetic practice.

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: George Puttenham was an English courtier and writer of criticism. He was born about 1529 and died about 1590. He is remembered for one book, The Arte of English Poesie. That book teaches how English verse should be made, measured, and ornamented.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET asks this book under Unit II (Poetry) and in criticism matching questions. Students must link 1589, the poet as maker, and the three books.

fields.label: Memory Tip & Exam Traps

items.title: Edmund Spenser (c. 1552–1599)
items.meta: Elizabethan Period · British & Irish Literature · 18 PYQs

fields.label: Writer Name
fields.value: Edmund Spenser

fields.label: L1 One-Line Flash Anchor
fields.value: Shepheardes Calender (1579); Faerie Queene I–III (1590), IV–VI (1596); Amoretti and Epithalamion (1595).

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: In the reign of Queen Elizabeth I, Edmund Spenser was a major English poet. He was born in London about 1552 and died on 13 January 1599. He studied at Cambridge and later served the English crown in Ireland. His long poem The Faerie Queene praises the queen through knights and virtues.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET asks Spenser in Unit 2 (Poetry). Questions match titles with years. They also ask which knight stands for which virtue.

fields.label: L1 One-Line Flash Anchor
fields.value: Euphues (1578); Euphues and His England (1580); Endymion (printed 1591); Gallathea (printed 1592).

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: John Lyly was an Elizabethan writer of prose and of court comedy. He was born in Kent about 1554 and died in London in November 1606. He studied at Magdalen College, Oxford. His decorated prose is called euphuism (a balanced style full of clever comparisons).

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET asks Lyly under Unit 1 (Drama) and also for prose style. Questions ask the year 1578 and the word euphuism. They also ask which plays flatter Queen Elizabeth.

items.title: Philip Sidney (1554–1586)

fields.label: L1 One-Line Flash Anchor
fields.value: Astrophil and Stella (1591); Defence of Poesy (written c. 1579–1580; printed 1595); Arcadia (1590, revised version 1593). Most major works appeared posthumously.

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Sir Philip Sidney was an English poet, courtier, and soldier. He was born at Penshurst on 30 November 1554. He died of a battle wound at Arnhem on 17 October 1586. None of his major books was printed while he lived.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET asks Sidney in Unit 3 (Fiction) and in criticism. Questions match titles with years. They also ask what kind of poetry he ranks highest.

items.title: Richard Hooker (1554–1600)
items.meta: Elizabethan Period · British & Irish Literature · 1 PYQs

fields.label: Writer Name
fields.value: Richard Hooker

fields.label: L1 One-Line Flash Anchor
fields.value: Books I–IV (1593); Book V (1597); remaining books published posthumously in 1648.

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Richard Hooker was an English priest and theologian (a writer on God and the church). He was born at Heavitree, near Exeter, in 1554. He died at Bishopsbourne in Kent in November 1600. His great book defends the Church of England by scripture, custom, and reason.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET asks Hooker under Unit 4 (prose that is not a story). The database calls him a poetry author, which is a mistake. Questions ask which books came out in 1593 and 1597, and which books came after his death.

fields.label: Memory Tip & Exam Traps
fields.value: Laws of Ecclesiastical Polity. Books 1 to 4 in 1593, Book 5 in 1597, later books after his death. | Books I–IV (1593); Book V (1597); remaining books published posthumously in 1648.

items.title: George Peele (c. 1556–1596)
items.meta: Elizabethan Period · British & Irish Literature · 2 PYQs

fields.label: Writer Name
fields.value: George Peele

fields.label: L1 One-Line Flash Anchor
fields.value: Old Wives’ Tale printed 1595; David and Bethsabe printed 1599.

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: George Peele was an English poet and playwright. He was baptized in London on 25 July 1556 and buried on 9 November 1596. He studied at Oxford and then wrote plays and city pageants (public festival shows). He belonged to the University Wits (university men who wrote for the new London stages).

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET asks Peele in Unit 1 (Drama). Questions place him with the University Wits and ask which play is his. The Old Wives' Tale is the usual text. David and Bethsabe is the Bible play printed after his death.

fields.label: Memory Tip & Exam Traps

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Robert Greene was an English playwright and writer of prose romances (long stories in ordinary prose). He was baptised in Norwich in 1558 and died in London in 1592. items.title: Thomas Kyd (1558–1594)

fields.label: Writer Name
fields.value: Thomas Kyd

fields.label: L1 One-Line Flash Anchor
fields.value: Probably performed c. 1587–1590; printed 1592, with later additions.

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Thomas Kyd was an English playwright of the Elizabethan age (the reign of Elizabeth I). He was baptized in London on 6 November 1558, and he died in 1594. He went to Merchant Taylors' School and did not attend a university. His Spanish Tragedy began the English revenge tragedy (a play about paying back a murder).

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET asks Kyd in Unit 1 (Drama). Questions link The Spanish Tragedy with Seneca and with Hamlet. They also test the 1592 print and the revenge tragedy type.

fields.value: Thomas Norton and Thomas Sackville were English lawyers, statesmen, and writers. Norton was born in 1532 and died in 1584. Sackville was born in 1536 and died in 1608. Together they wrote Gorboduc, the first English tragedy in blank verse (unrhymed lines of ten syllables).

fields.value: Francis Bacon was an English lawyer, statesman, and philosopher. He was born in London on 22 January 1561 and died on 9 April 1626. Under King James I he rose to Lord Chancellor, then fell for taking bribes. He is remembered for his essays and for a new way of studying nature.

items.title: William Shakespeare (1564–1616)
items.meta: Jacobean Period · British & Irish Literature · 56 PYQs

fields.label: Writer Name
fields.value: William Shakespeare

fields.label: L1 One-Line Flash Anchor
fields.value: Venus and Adonis (1593); Lucrece (1594); Sonnets (1609). Sonnets likely composed earlier; sequence/order and dedication remain debated.

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: William Shakespeare (1564-1616) was an English poet, playwright, and actor, universally regarded as the greatest dramatist in world literature. Born in Stratford-upon-Avon, he worked in London as an actor, writer, and part-owner of the Lord Chamberlain's Men (later the King's Men). He wrote approximately 37 to 39 plays, 154 sonnets, and two long narrative poems.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: Shakespeare is the single most heavily tested author in UGC NET (35+ direct past questions). Questions test chronological ordering of plays, Quarto vs. 1623 First Folio facts, famous critic quotes on Shakespeare, literary sources (Plutarch, Holinshed, Lodge, Greene, Cinthio), fools/clowns across plays, cross-dressing heroines, and modern novels that took their titles from Shakespearean lines.

fields.label: Memory Tip & Exam Traps
fields.value: 1582 married Anne Hathaway -> 1592 Greene's 'Upstart Crow' -> 1593-94 Venus & Lucrece -> 1609 Quarto of 154 Sonnets (Thorpe) -> 1616 Died -> 1623 First Folio (36 plays by Heminges & Condell, missing Pericles & Two Noble Kinsmen). | Venus and Adonis (1593); Lucrece (1594); Sonnets (1609). Sonnets likely composed earlier; sequence/order and dedication remain debated. | See dedicated Shakespeare chronology below; performance and quarto/folio dates often differ. | 36 plays in First Folio (1623); 154 Sonnets (1609). | Defining tragedies are Jacobean. The 1590s comedies and histories come before 1603.

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Thomas Nashe was an English playwright and satirist (a writer who mocks faults). He was baptised in Lowestoft in 1567 and died about 1601. He studied at Cambridge and then wrote in London. He belonged to the University Wits (university men who wrote for the stage and the press).

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Ben Jonson was an English playwright, poet, and actor. He was born about 1572 and died in 1637. In 1598 he killed a man in a duel and was spared after reading a Bible verse. He became the leading comic writer of King James's reign.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET asks Jonson in Unit 1 (Drama) and Unit 2 (Poetry). Questions match comedies with years. They also ask about humours and the 1616 folio.

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: John Donne was an English poet and a priest of the Church of England. He was born in London in 1572 and died on 31 March 1631. He was raised a Roman Catholic, then secretly married Anne More in 1601 and lost his post. From 1621 until his death he was dean (head priest) of Saint Paul's Cathedral.

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Thomas Dekker was an English playwright and writer of pamphlets (short prose pieces). He was born in London about 1572 and died about 1632. He wrote lively plays and prose about ordinary London people. He often wrote with other playwrights, and he spent years in prison for debt.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET asks Dekker in Unit 1 (Drama). Questions name The Shoemaker's Holiday as his citizen comedy (a funny play about London workers). Old Fortunatus is the magic play of the same year. Both were printed in 1600.

fields.value: Under King James I, John Marston was a playwright and satirist (a writer who mocks vice). He was baptised in Oxfordshire on 7 October 1576 and died in London in 1634. fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Francis Beaumont and John Fletcher were English playwrights who wrote plays together. Fletcher was born in 1579 and died in 1625. Beaumont was born in the mid 1580s and died in 1616. They wrote for the King's Men (Shakespeare's acting company).

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET asks them in Unit 1 (Drama). Questions match a play to its writers, its year, and its type. Philaster is the model tragicomedy. The Knight of the Burning Pestle is usually Beaumont alone.

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: John Webster was an English playwright of the Jacobean age (the reign of James I). He was born in London about 1580, and he died about 1632. fields.value: Thomas Middleton was an English playwright and poet. He was baptised in London in 1580 and died in 1627. He wrote city comedy (a funny play about London money and marriage). He also wrote harsh tragedy, often with William Rowley.

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: In the reign of King Charles I, John Ford was an English playwright. He was baptised at Ilsington in Devon on 17 April 1586. He lived at the Middle Temple in London, a college for lawyers. His last known play was printed in 1639, and no sure death date exists.

fields.value: Thomas Hobbes was an English thinker and writer on government. He was born in 1588 and died in 1679. He spent most of his working life as tutor to the Cavendish family. The English Civil War shaped his case for a strong ruler.

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Robert Herrick was an English priest and poet of short lyrics (poems of personal feeling). He was baptized in 1591 and died in 1674. He served as vicar of Dean Prior in Devon, except during the civil war years. He is a Cavalier poet (a royal poet of light, graceful songs).

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET asks Herrick in Unit 2 (Poetry). Questions place him with the Cavalier poets and with Ben Jonson. Gather ye rosebuds is the line to know. Hesperides and Noble Numbers share the 1648 book.

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: George Herbert was an English priest and a religious poet. He was born in Wales on 3 April 1593 and died at Bemerton on 1 March 1633. He left hopes of a court career and served a small country parish. His English poems were printed in 1633, just after he died.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET asks Herbert in Unit 2 (Poetry). Questions place The Temple in 1633 and group him with the metaphysical poets. They also ask about Easter Wings, The Collar, and Love.

fields.value: Izaak Walton wrote biographies (stories of real lives) and a famous fishing book. He was baptised at Stafford in 1593, and he died at Winchester in 1683. fields.value: Andrew Marvell was an English poet and member of Parliament. He was born at Winestead on 31 March 1621 and died in London on 16 August 1678. He worked with the poet John Milton in Cromwell's government. Most of his lyrics were printed in 1681, after his death.

fields.value: Anne Bradstreet was an English poet who settled in Massachusetts. She was born in 1612 and died on 16 September 1672. She sailed over with her husband Simon Bradstreet and her father Thomas Dudley. She was one of the first poets published from the American colonies.

fields.value: UGC NET asks Bradstreet under Unit II (Poetry) as an early American poet. Questions match The Tenth Muse with 1650. A common trap is to call her a British metaphysical poet (a poet of witty comparisons, like Donne).
